case_name: Diksha Sharma & Anr v. Navneet Kumar
facts_of_case: FIR sought to be quashed against petitioner-accused for alleged indecent behavior and stalking. Complainant alleged repeated pressure to marry and showing of pistol in January 2018.

legal_principles.principle: Power under Section 482 Cr.P.C should not be exercised in cases involving heinous and serious offences.
legal_principles.held: Hon'ble Apex Court has specifically held that power under Section 482 Cr.P.C is not to be exercised in the cases which involve heinous and serious offences of mental depravity or offences like murder, rape, dacoity, etc., as such offences are not private in nature and have a serious impact on society?
cited_cases: Narinder Singh and others versus State of Punjab and another, (2014) 6 SCC 466
use_in: cases involving murder or serious crimes

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party seeking quashing of FIR to demonstrate that there are no reasonable grounds for proceeding with the prosecution.
legal_principles.held: No fruitful purpose would be served in case FIR as well as consequent proceedings pending adjudication in the competent court of law are allowed to sustain.

outcome.final_order: FIR No.33 of 2019, dated 03.03.2019, under Sections 354, 354-D, 506 & 201 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 27 of Arms Act, registered at Police Station Shimla West, Shimla, H.P., quashed.

use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for quashing an FIR
